name: Sihon
overview: Sihon was a male king of the Amorites during the time of the Exodus. He ruled over the Amorite tribe and is specifically noted as the King of the Amorites in Numbers 21:21. His reign represents a significant opposition to the Israelites as they journeyed to the Promised Land.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Sihon' is recorded as a proper name without a given meaning. He is also referred to by titles such as 'King of the Amorites' and 'King of Heshbon,' which identify his rulership over the Amorite people and the city of Heshbon, respectively. These titles emphasize his political and territorial authority during his time.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Sihon as a descendant of Amor, linking him to the Amorite lineage. Beyond this inferred relationship, the Bible does not provide further details about his family or other personal relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Sihon is significant in the biblical narrative as a key Amorite king who opposed the Israelites during the Exodus. His confrontation with the Israelites reflects the challenges they faced in entering the Promised Land. As King of the Amorites and ruler of Heshbon, his resistance marks an important moment in Israel's journey under God's guidance.
